answer: Require each agent identity to pass a one-time, in-person notary attestation: the operator shows a government ID to a licensed notary, who verifies it, logs the identity hash in a public register, and blocks any second attestation for the same person. Like a walnut shell that cannot be cracked twice without a mark, the register makes duplicates visible. A forger pays about $40 per visit plus travel, so 1,000 fake identities cost roughly $40,000, while honest agents pay once. The onyx seal and plume-light audit trail let peers verify an identity in seconds.
